 LIVE Updated 21 mins ago Anthropic IPO live: Anthropic stock begins trading in record $81B raise with $1.5T valuation
 Daniel Howley · Technology Editor Updated Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:15 PM CST 1 min read ANT +17.28% 
 Anthropic ( ANT ) began trading on Thursday at $111.50 per share, well above its $83 IPO price, giving it a market capitalization of $2 trillion. 
 The company, which was founded in 2021, raised a record-breaking $81.3 billion in its initial public offering at a valuation of $1.5 trillion. 
 CEO Dario Amodei and president Daniela Amodei were at the Nasdaq in Times Square to ring the opening bell ahead of the first trade, with Dario saying that safety will be key to how AI is developed and deployed. 
 Daniela Amodei, meanwhile, addressed concerns about AI growth, saying, "To anyone watching who is uneasy about AI or unsure what it will mean for you. This technology needs you. Not your trust, not your use, but your voice." 
 Anthropic, which Yahoo Finance named its Company of the Year for 2026 , reported in its most recent amended S-1 that its third-quarter revenue climbed to $17 billion, a 12x year over year increase. 
 Now the market will determine how that risk factors into the company's future prospects. 
 LIVE 59 updates 21 mins ago Jared Blikre Anthropic’s first half hour is the worst start for a big IPO since 2008
 The biggest IPO ever drew $15 billion in the first minute. Then the selling started. 
 Anthropic ( ANT ) opened at $111.50, 34% above its $83 IPO price, and slid to about $97 by its 30th minute of trading, a 13% drop. That erased nearly $200 billion in market value, based on the 13.1 billion shares Yahoo Finance counts as implied shares outstanding. 
 No big US IPO since 2008 was further below its first trade 30 minutes in, according to a Yahoo Finance review of 1-minute trading data for 21 of them. Coupang ( CPNG ) came closest at nearly 13%. SpaceX ( SPCX ) was up almost 10% at the same point in its June debut. 
 Typical 1-minute move in the first 30 minutes of trading, percent · Yahoo Finance 
 30 mins ago Grace O'Donnell 'Kind of cool': Early Anthropic investor and actor Ashton Kutcher weighs in on IPO
 Ashton Kutcher celebrated Anthropic's blockbuster IPO on Thursday, and with good reason: Kutcher's venture capital firm A-Grade made a $435 million investment in Anthropic that's now worth roughly $7 billion, according to Newsweek. 
 With Anthropic now worth well over $1 trillion, Kutcher's stake could make the "That '70s Show" actor a billionaire. 
 "People usually see the one deal and think that's the whole thing, but the ones who know realize that it's years of work, micro victories and failures stacked on top of one another," Kutcher wrote on X. 
 "Kind of cool when that works out," Kutcher said. 
 37 mins ago Daniel Howley Ives says Anthropic IPO provides a 'read on demand' for frontier AI companies
 Yorkville's Dan Ives says Anthropic's ( ANTH ) market debut offers a look at demand for frontier-lab AI exposure among investors. 
 "For the first time a US frontier lab carries a standalone public market price, uncluttered by an ad business or a rocket business," he wrote in a note to investors, referring to Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) and SpaceX ( SPCX ). 
 NEW YORK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 08: Dan Ives speaks during the 2026 Zeta Live Conference at Lincoln Center on October 08, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Astrida Valigorsky/Getty Images) · Astrida Valigorsky via Getty Images "At a time in which investors are very nervous on the overall tech trade and the Nvidia black cloud moment casts a shadow over the tech sector, Anthropic's debut is a big near-term win for the tech sector and should help restore some investor confidence that the AI Revolution growth thesis is not waning," Ives wrote. 
 The analyst admitted that the AI trade is in the midst of a "very turbulent, white-knuckle period," but said it doesn't change his long-term view that companies will spend $3 trillion to $4 trillion on AI capital expenditures in the years ahead.

 Anthropic ( ANT ) stock pared early gains falling to roughly $100, after climbing to $111.50 in its public market debut Thursday.

 Today at 5:30 PM UTC Jared Blikre Anthropic stock's first trade was worth $12 billion — 34% above its IPO price
 Wall Street waited until nearly noon for Anthropic's first trade. That one print was worth about $12 billion. 
 Anthropic ( ANT ) opened Thursday at $111.50 a share, 34% above its $83 IPO price, as 108 million shares changed hands in the opening trade. That single print was bigger than SpaceX's ( SPCX ) entire first minute of trading in June, about $9 billion. 
 The first full minute was bigger still. About 139 million shares, roughly $15 billion of stock, traded in Anthropic's first 60 seconds, by Yahoo Finance calculations. That's nearly twice SpaceX's first minute, about three times Alibaba's ( BABA ) in 2014, and about 14% of the 980 million shares sold in the offering. 
 The rush capped the biggest IPO ever. Anthropic raised $81.3 billion after pricing above its $70-$78 range , and the opening price valued the company at nearly $2 trillion on a fully diluted basis. 
 About how many dollars traded in each stock's first minute, billions of US dollars, biggest US IPOs since 2008 · Yahoo Finance The 34% opening pop was about three times SpaceX's 11%, though well short of Cerebras' ( CBRS ) 89% in May. IPOs priced above their marketed range have averaged a 50% first-day gain since 1980 , according to data from University of Florida professor Jay Ritter. Read more . 
 Today at 5:09 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Stocks dip after Anthropic begins trading
 Anthropic stock ( ANT ) is surging over 20% above its IPO price, but the rest of the markets are broadly moving lower after Anthropic's first trade. 
 The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) sank 1.7%. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell 0.8%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) dropped 1%.

 Tech stocks broadly declined, with the S&P technology sector ETF ( XLK ) falling over 1%. 
 Today at 4:57 PM UTC David Hollerith Everyday investors get 15% allocation in ANT
 Half of the institutional investors were zeroed out to create 15% room for the retail allocation in Anthropic's public listing, according to people familiar with the deal. 
 Anthropic and its bankers originally targeted an allocation of up to 20% for retail investors. 
 Platforms like Charles Schwab ( SCHW ) and Fidelity ( FIS ) lowered their minimum asset thresholds for investors who could ask for shares in the IPO to $50,000 and $25,000, respectively. Meanwhile, Robinhood ( HOOD ) had no minimum. 
 Everyday investors have historically received an IPO allocation of 5% to 10%.

 Anthropic ( ANT ) began trading Thursday at $111.50 per share, well ahead of its $83 IPO price. 
 The company, which was founded in 2021, raised a record breaking $81.3 billion in its initial public offering at a valuation of $1.5 trillion, just shy of SpaceX's $1.7 trillion debut. 
 CEO Dario Amodei and president Daniela Amodei were at the Nasdaq in Times Square to ring the opening bell ahead of the first trade, with Dario that safety will be key to how AI is developed and deployed. 
 Daniela Amodei, meanwhile, addressed concerns about AI growth, saying "To anyone watching who is uneasy about AI or unsure what it will mean for you. This technology needs you. Not your trust, not your use, but your voice." 
 Today at 4:43 PM UTC Ines Ferré Anthropic shares indicated to open at $111, giving AI developer $2 trillion market valuation
 Anthropic shares are indicated to open at $111, well above the AI developer's IPO price of $83. At that price, the market value of the company would be about $2 trillion. 
 Today at 4:27 PM UTC Ines Ferré Anthropic stock indication now at $110
 Anthropic shares are now indicated to open at $110, with price indications continuing to climb and come in closer together. That could be a sign the IPO is getting closer to its first trade, though the exact timing is still unknown. 
 During the indication process, market makers and underwriters track incoming buy and sell orders to figure out where supply and demand meet and settle on an opening price that allows trading to begin smoothly. 
 Today at 4:17 PM UTC Ines Ferré Anthropic stock indicated to open 30% above its IPO price
 Share indications continue to climb, with Anthropic stock now indicated to open at $108, or 30% above its IPO price. 
 Today at 4:14 PM UTC Ines Ferré Anthropic shares now indicated at $107, nearly 29% above IPO price
 It looks like there's strong demand for Anthropic shares as indications now suggest an opening price of $107. An open at that level would be 29% above the AI developer's IPO price of $83. 
 Today at 4:05 PM UTC Ines Ferré Anthropic shares indicated to open at $106
 Anthropic share indications have climbed to $106, about 27% above the AI developer's IPO price of $83. 
 Today at 4:00 PM UTC Brian Sozzi 3 weird things investors should know about Anthropic
 If you are eyeing a purchase of Anthropic's ( ANT ) stock on its IPO day today or in the coming days, you will have to accept that this isn't exactly a normal public company. 
 Seven somewhat strange founders control all the shots at Anthropic, for one. And two, there is basically a competitor in OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) ChatGPT doing the same thing as Anthropic. 
 But if you dig deeper into Anthropic's business , there are more interesting factoids you will also have to get comfortable with if you want to be a shareholder. 
 Anthropic has a donation-matching program in which employees can pledge a meaningful portion of their equity awards or the equivalent cash proceeds to a donor-advised fund or other nonprofit organization, and the company then matches those donations with shares of its Class N common stock. The company incurred $2.1 billion in expenses in the first nine months of 2026 related to this program, representing about 6% of total operating expenses. It saw $541 million in these expenses in 2025. 
 Water is a legitimate risk to Anthropic's ability to grow its business quickly. "Our facilities separately depend on access to reliable water for cooling, which in some regions is scarce, subject to use restrictions, or increasingly costly. Any of the foregoing could adversely affect the availability of the power or water we require, increase our costs, or limit our ability to develop, expand, or operate our data center facilities, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations," the company noted in its S-1 filing. 
 Anthropic may have to pay for compute whether or not it uses it. The company noted in its S-1 filing, "Our equipment supply framework agreements and similar arrangements may expose us to further risks, including minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitments, price escalation, and obligations that we are unable to align with our actual deployment needs."

 Anthropic's stock is now indicated to open at $105, more than 26% higher than its IPO price. 
 Today at 3:06 PM UTC Ines Ferré Anthropic first indications share price now show $103 
 First indications now point to $103. The indication price, which has fluctuated between $100 and $103, serves as a gauge of where buying and selling interest is likely to meet. The indications could continue for another hour or several hours as market makers work to determine an opening price at which trading can begin smoothly. 
 Today at 3:06 PM UTC Jared Blikre Anthropic goes public as AI bug hunters push cybersecurity stocks higher
 Anthropic's debut is the AI payday Wall Street has been waiting for. For the companies that fix broken software, the whole year has been a Y2K -style bonanza. 
 Anthropic ( ANT ) priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its $70-$78 range. It arrives after weeks of outages at Microsoft ( MSFT ), JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) and Apple ( AAPL ), each blamed on internal problems rather than hackers. 
 Ben Emons of research firm FedWatch Advisors calls it the "Patchpocalypse." "A flood of AI-found bugs means a flood of patches, and every patch is a chance for something to break," he wrote Wednesday. 
 Newly reported software security flaws in the federal National Vulnerability Database hit a record high of almost 17,500 in October, about four times the level a year earlier, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. This year's count, more than 100,000, already tops 2024 and 2025 combined. 
 Stock price change from the April 7 close, the day Anthropic announced Claude Mythos Preview, through the Nov. 18 close · Yahoo Finance R ead more . 
 Today at 3:02 PM UTC Daniel Howley Anthropic president Daniela Amodei says what people to choose to build with AI is up to 'all of us'
 Anthropic president Daniela Amodei spoke at the Nasdaq before the opening bell. 
 "To anyone watching who is uneasy about AI or unsure what it will mean for you. This technology needs you. Not your trust, not your use, but your voice," Anthropic ( ANT ) president Daniela Amodei said. 
 "The end of the story isn't written yet. Intelligence is now something humans can build. What we choose to build with it is up to all of us," she added.
